sets.title: Similes & proverbs · 40 items
sets.instruction: Choose the option that completes the simile or proverb correctly.

questions.q: After the long hike, Ravi slept like a __________.
questions.tip: 'Slept like a log' means slept very deeply.

questions.q: The twins are as alike as two __________ in a pod.
questions.tip: The simile is 'as alike as two peas in a pod'.

questions.q: My grandfather is as fit as a __________ at seventy.
questions.tip: 'As fit as a fiddle' means in excellent health.

questions.q: She went as white as a __________ when she heard the news.
questions.tip: 'As white as a sheet' describes a face pale with shock.

questions.q: The little boy was as quiet as a __________ during the test.
questions.tip: 'As quiet as a mouse' is the set simile.

questions.q: The soup was as cold as __________ by the time we ate.
questions.tip: 'As cold as ice' is the fixed comparison.

questions.q: He is as stubborn as a __________.
questions.tip: 'As stubborn as a mule' means refusing to change.

questions.q: Her explanation was as clear as __________.
questions.tip: 'As clear as crystal' means perfectly clear.

questions.q: The old man's hands were as rough as __________.
questions.tip: 'As rough as sandpaper' describes a coarse surface.

questions.q: Don't count your __________ before they hatch.
questions.tip: The proverb warns against assuming success too early.

questions.q: A __________ in time saves nine.
questions.tip: Fixing a small problem early prevents a big one.

questions.q: Too many __________ spoil the broth.
questions.tip: Too many people interfering ruins the result.

questions.q: Actions speak louder than __________.
questions.tip: What you do matters more than what you say.

questions.q: Don't judge a book by its __________.
The early __________ catches the worm.
questions.tip: Those who act first gain the advantage.

questions.q: Practice makes __________.
Where there's a will, there's a __________.
Two __________ don't make a right.
questions.tip: Returning bad behaviour does not justify it.

questions.q: Look before you __________.
A leopard cannot change its __________.
questions.tip: People rarely change their basic nature.

questions.q: Rome was not built in a __________.
Strike while the __________ is hot.
Every __________ has a silver lining.
questions.tip: Every difficulty has something good in it.

questions.q: Let sleeping __________ lie.
questions.tip: Do not stir up an old problem.

questions.q: Birds of a __________ flock together.
The __________ is mightier than the sword.
questions.tip: Writing has more power than force.

questions.q: Honesty is the best __________.
questions.tip: Telling the truth is always wisest.

questions.q: Beggars cannot be __________.
questions.tip: Those in need must accept what is offered.

questions.q: Make __________ while the sun shines.
questions.tip: Use a good opportunity while it lasts.

questions.q: He was as busy as a __________ all afternoon.
questions.tip: 'As busy as a bee' means working hard.

questions.q: The thief was as slippery as an __________ and slid away through the crowd.
questions.tip: 'As slippery as an eel' is the set simile.

questions.q: My sister eats like a __________ when she gets home.
questions.tip: 'Eats like a horse' means eats a great deal.

questions.q: He is as blind as a __________ without his glasses.
questions.tip: 'As blind as a bat' is the fixed comparison.

questions.q: The answer was as plain as the __________ on your face.
questions.tip: 'As plain as the nose on your face' means obvious.

questions.q: A __________ of all trades is a master of none.
questions.tip: Someone who does everything does nothing excellently.

questions.q: Don't put all your __________ in one basket.
questions.tip: Do not risk everything on one plan.

questions.q: It is no use crying over spilt __________.
questions.tip: There is no point regretting what cannot be undone.

questions.q: She felt as light as a __________ after the results came out.
questions.tip: 'As light as a feather' is the set simile.

questions.q: The new boy stood out like a __________ thumb.
questions.tip: 'Like a sore thumb' means very noticeable.

questions.q: Better late than __________.
questions.tip: Arriving late is better than not arriving.

sets.title: Homophones · words that sound the same
sets.instruction: These pairs sound identical but mean different things. Type the correct one.

questions.q: The wind __________ (blew / blue) so hard that the umbrella turned inside out.
questions.tip: 'Blew' is the past of 'blow'; 'blue' is the colour.

questions.q: Please write your name on the line __________ (their / there / they're) is a space.
questions.tip: 'There is' points out that something exists.

questions.q: __________ (Their / There / They're) bags were left in the corridor.
__________ (Their / There / They're) coming over after lunch.
I could not hear the announcement because the fan was __________ (to / too / two) loud.
We walked __________ (to / too / two) the bus stop together.
She has __________ (to / too / two) younger brothers.
The dog wagged __________ (its / it's) tail.
__________ (Its / It's) almost time for recess.
__________ (Your / You're) shoes are under the bed.
__________ (Your / You're) going to enjoy this book.
We stood on the __________ (peace / piece) of cardboard to keep our feet dry.
questions.tip: A 'piece' is a part of something.

questions.q: After the argument they finally made __________ (peace / piece).
questions.tip: 'Peace' means calm or the end of conflict.

questions.q: The nurse checked his __________ (hole / whole) arm for a rash.
There was a __________ (hole / whole) in the fence behind the shed.
The referee decided the tackle was __________ (fair / fare) and waved play on.
questions.tip: 'Fair' means just; a 'fare' is the money you pay for a journey.

questions.q: My grandmother paid the bus __________ (fair / fare) with her card.
questions.tip: A 'fare' is the cost of a journey.

questions.q: From the top of the hill we could see the whole __________ (plane / plain).
questions.tip: A 'plain' is flat land; a 'plane' flies.

questions.q: She took a quick __________ (peak / peek) at the last page.
questions.tip: A 'peek' is a quick look; a 'peak' is the top of a mountain.

questions.q: The __________ (weather / whether) forecast promised thunderstorms.
I could not decide __________ (weather / whether) to go.
The recipe calls for __________ (flour / flower) and eggs.
She planted one __________ (flour / flower) in each pot.
My shoes were __________ (allowed / aloud) in the studio.
Please read the paragraph __________ (allowed / aloud).
The __________ (principal / principle) spoke at assembly.
questions.tip: The 'principal' is the head of a school.

questions.q: The __________ (principal / principle) reason for the delay was the weather.
questions.tip: 'Principal' can also mean main or chief.

questions.q: He hurt his __________ (waist / waste) lifting the crate.
questions.tip: The 'waist' is part of the body.

questions.q: Do not __________ (waist / waste) the leftover rice.
The bus fare __________ (rose / rows) to a dollar last month.
We sat in the last two __________ (rose / rows) of the hall.
She __________ (passed / past) the ball to me.
We walked __________ (passed / past) the old cinema.
Our team __________ (one / won) the final by a single goal.
questions.tip: 'Won' is the past of 'win'; 'one' is the number.

questions.q: He was too __________ (weak / week) to finish the race.
We have swimming lessons twice a __________ (weak / week).
She __________ (threw / through) the ball over the fence.
The cat squeezed __________ (threw / through) the gap.
questions.tip: 'Through' means from one side to the other.

questions.q: They stood in a __________ (stationary / stationery) queue outside the shop.
I bought a ruler at the __________ (stationary / stationery) shop.

sets.title: Compound words · 30 items
sets.instruction: Complete each compound word. Type the missing part only.

questions.q: A place where you park cars is a car __________.
questions.tip: 'Car park' is written as two words in British English but functions as one idea.

questions.q: A brush for your teeth is a __________brush.
A room where you take a bath is a __________room.
Light from the sun is __________light.
A cloth used to dry dishes is a dish __________.
The time when the sun goes down is __________set.
Someone who keeps goal in a game is a __________keeper.
A book for writing notes is a __________book.
A path for walking beside a road is a __________path.
A storm with thunder is a __________storm.
The part of the day after noon is called the after__________.
Paper used for writing letters is __________paper.
A yard behind a house is a __________yard.
A cake eaten at teatime is a tea__________.
A person who fights fires is a fire__________.
Work done at home after school is home__________.
A bag carried on your back is a back__________.
A board on which you write with chalk is a black__________.
Rain that falls heavily is a down__________.
A cut made by paper is a paper __________.
questions.tip: 'Paper cut' is written as two words.

questions.q: Water that falls from the sky over a year is measured as rain__________.
The time of day when you eat lunch is lunch__________.
The box you carry your food in is a lunch__________.
A coat you put on in wet weather is a rain__________.
A bridge built so people can walk over a road is a foot__________.
The place where two roads cross is a cross__________.
questions.tip: A 'crossroads' is one word and always ends in s.

questions.q: A shop that sells and repairs bicycles is a bicycle __________.
questions.tip: 'Bicycle shop' is written as two words.

questions.q: Someone who reads a great deal is a book__________.
Food that remains after a meal is called left__________.
questions.tip: 'Leftovers' is one word and is always plural.

questions.q: The sill at the bottom of a window is a window__________.

sets.title: Describing feelings & character · 50 words for composition
sets.instruction: Every one of these words can replace a tired word such as 'happy', 'sad' or 'angry' in a composition. Choose the best fit.

questions.q: After weeks of practice, Devi was __________ when she heard she had come first, and could not stop grinning.
He was __________ rather than excited about the prize, as he had expected it.
questions.tip: 'Indifferent' means showing no interest either way.

questions.q: The loss left her __________ for days.
questions.tip: 'Dejected' means low in spirits after a disappointment.

questions.q: The referee's decision went against his team and left the coach __________.
questions.tip: 'Seething' means boiling with anger held in.

questions.q: She gave a __________ smile after admitting she had forgotten.
questions.tip: 'Sheepish' means embarrassed at one's own mistake.

questions.q: The little boy was __________ by the size of the hall.
questions.tip: 'Overawed' means made to feel small by something impressive.

questions.q: He looked __________ at the photograph of his old school.
questions.tip: 'Wistful' means sadly longing for something past. Because 'looked at' here means 'gazed at', the adverb 'wistfully' is needed.

questions.q: Her __________ tone made everyone stop talking at once.
The boy was __________ about his chances and told everybody so.
questions.tip: 'Boastful' means speaking too proudly about oneself.

questions.q: Despite winning, she remained __________ about her achievement.
The __________ child hid behind her mother's legs.
He was __________ enough to enter the burning flat.
questions.tip: 'Foolhardy' means brave without thinking of the danger.

questions.q: She is a __________ worker who never leaves a task unfinished.
His __________ reply surprised us, as he is usually so polite.
The old lady was __________ to everyone who passed her stall, greeting each one with a smile and a joke.
He remained __________ throughout the argument and never raised his voice.
The news left her __________ and unable to speak.
questions.tip: 'Dumbfounded' means so astonished that one cannot speak.

questions.q: The children grew __________ as the wait went on.
questions.tip: 'Restless' means unable to keep still through impatience.

questions.q: His __________ behaviour at the museum embarrassed his parents.
questions.tip: 'Unruly' means badly behaved and hard to control.

questions.q: She was __________ about the missing money and questioned everybody.
The dog's owner was __________ when it was found unhurt.
He wore a __________ expression all through the funeral.
The boy was __________ after being left out of the team.
Her __________ manner put the nervous new pupil at ease.
He was __________ to admit that he had been wrong.
The __________ crowd pushed towards the stage.
After the long illness she looked __________ but cheerful.
His __________ questions showed he had read the whole book.
She was __________ by the unfairness of the decision.
The __________ boy shared his lunch without being asked.
He felt a __________ sense of guilt long afterwards.
questions.tip: 'Nagging' means persistent and impossible to ignore.

questions.q: Her __________ laughter filled the corridor, and soon everybody else was laughing too.
The __________ silence after the announcement was worse than shouting.
He is __________ about his stamp collection and can talk of nothing else.
She gave a __________ nod, plainly annoyed at being stopped, and walked on.
The __________ old man refused all offers of help.
His face was __________ with pride as his daughter collected the trophy.
She was __________ at having forgotten her friend's birthday.
The team was __________ after losing four matches in a row.
questions.tip: 'Demoralised' means having lost confidence and hope.

questions.q: He is __________ enough to notice when somebody is upset.
The __________ cat would not come near anybody.
questions.tip: 'Wary' means cautious because of possible danger.

questions.q: Her __________ apology did not convince anyone.
He was __________ with relief when his sister answered the phone.
questions.tip: 'Weak with relief' describes the body going limp when a fear passes.

questions.q: The __________ boy volunteered for every duty.
She was __________ by the kindness of a stranger.
questions.tip: 'Humbled' means made to feel modest by somebody's goodness.

questions.q: His __________ remarks upset the whole group.
questions.tip: 'Tactless' means careless of other people's feelings.

questions.q: The __________ pupil asked to redo the work she had rushed.
questions.tip: 'Conscientious' means taking care to do things properly.

questions.q: He felt __________ about the whole affair and changed the subject.
Her __________ gaze never left the door.
questions.tip: 'Unwavering' means steady and never moving away.

questions.q: He was __________ that nobody had noticed his mistake.

sets.title: Vivid verbs · show, don't tell
sets.instruction: Each sentence uses a weak verb. Choose the precise verb that a marker would reward.

questions.q: Instead of 'walked slowly and painfully', write that the injured runner __________ to the finish.
questions.tip: 'Hobbled' shows both slowness and pain in one word.

questions.q: Instead of 'walked proudly', write that the winner __________ onto the stage.
Instead of 'walked quietly so as not to be heard', write that she __________ past the door.
questions.tip: 'Tiptoed' shows the care taken to be silent.

questions.q: Instead of 'walked with heavy, tired steps', write that we __________ up the last slope.
Instead of 'said angrily', write that the coach __________ at the defenders.
Instead of 'said very quietly', write that she __________ the answer.
Instead of 'said while crying', write that he __________ his apology.
questions.tip: 'Choked out' shows tears interrupting the words.

questions.q: Instead of 'said repeatedly and annoyingly', write that my brother __________ about the heat.
Instead of 'looked at for a long time', write that she __________ at the empty seat.
Instead of 'looked quickly', write that he __________ at the clock and stood up.
Instead of 'looked angrily', write that the prefect __________ at the latecomers.
Instead of 'looked with difficulty', write that she __________ through the dusty window.
Instead of 'ate quickly', write that the boys __________ their lunch.
Instead of 'ate in small amounts without appetite', write that she __________ her rice.
Instead of 'held tightly', write that he __________ the railing.
Instead of 'held gently', write that she __________ the injured bird.
Instead of 'threw carelessly', write that he __________ his bag onto the bed.
Instead of 'moved suddenly and quickly', write that the cat __________ under the sofa.
Instead of 'cried loudly', write that the toddler __________ in the supermarket.
Instead of 'cried quietly', write that she __________ into her sleeve.
Instead of 'laughed loudly', write that the class __________ at his joke.
Instead of 'laughed unkindly', write that the boys __________ at her answer.
Instead of 'rained heavily', write that the rain __________ down all afternoon.
Instead of 'the wind blew strongly', write that the wind __________ through the corridor.
Instead of 'shone brightly', write that the trophy __________ under the lights.
questions.tip: 'Gleamed' is a steady bright shine off a polished surface.

questions.q: Instead of 'the door closed loudly', write that the door __________ behind him.
questions.tip: 'Slammed' carries the noise and the temper.

questions.q: Instead of 'the water moved noisily', write that the water __________ over the rocks.
questions.tip: 'Gushed' shows fast, noisy flow; the others are all slow and quiet.

questions.q: Instead of 'the crowd made noise', write that the crowd __________ when the goal went in.
Instead of 'stood up quickly', write that she __________ to her feet.
Instead of 'sat down heavily', write that he __________ onto the bench.
Instead of 'walked into something by accident', write that he __________ into the door frame.
questions.tip: 'Crashed' shows the force of the collision.

questions.q: Instead of 'took quickly and roughly', write that she __________ the letter from my hand.
Instead of 'pushed through a crowd', write that we __________ our way to the front.
questions.tip: 'Elbowed' shows the physical effort of pushing.

questions.q: Instead of 'spoke without stopping', write that my aunt __________ about her holiday.
questions.tip: 'Rattled on' shows a stream of unstoppable talk.

questions.q: Instead of 'smelt strongly and unpleasantly', write that the bin __________ in the heat.
questions.tip: 'Reeked' means gave off a powerful bad smell.

questions.q: Instead of 'shook with cold', write that she __________ at the bus stop.
questions.tip: 'Shivered' shows the cold in the body.

questions.q: Instead of 'shook with fear', write that his hands __________ as he opened the envelope.
Instead of 'said suddenly without thinking', write that he __________ out the secret.
questions.tip: 'Blurted' shows words escaping before they can be stopped.

questions.q: Instead of 'breathed with difficulty', write that the runner __________ at the finish line.
Instead of 'the fire burnt low', write that the fire __________ in the grate.
questions.tip: 'Smouldered' means burning slowly without flame; the other three are loud or bright.

sets.title: Idioms in context (set 3) · 40 items
sets.instruction: Choose the meaning of the idiom as it is used in the sentence.

questions.q: When the teacher asked who had written on the desk, Ravi decided to come clean.
questions.tip: 'Come clean' means to admit the truth.

questions.q: The two brothers have been at loggerheads since the argument.
Learning the whole script in one night was a tall order.
questions.tip: 'A tall order' means a demanding request.

questions.q: My sister let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party.
questions.tip: 'Let the cat out of the bag' means to reveal a secret.

questions.q: He passed the examination by the skin of his teeth.
questions.tip: 'By the skin of his teeth' means only barely.

questions.q: The new pupil found the lessons a piece of cake.
questions.tip: 'A piece of cake' means very easy.

questions.q: Our coach told us not to throw in the towel after the first loss.
questions.tip: 'Throw in the towel' means to surrender.

questions.q: The two answers were like chalk and cheese.
She takes after her grandmother in both looks and temper.
The project has been on the back burner since March.
questions.tip: 'On the back burner' means set aside for later.

questions.q: Kumar has green fingers; his balcony is full of orchids.
questions.tip: 'Green fingers' (British and Singapore English) means a talent for gardening.

questions.q: Do not beat about the bush — tell me what happened.
questions.tip: 'Beat about the bush' means to avoid saying something directly.

questions.q: The captain's speech struck a chord with the whole team.
questions.tip: 'Struck a chord' means produced a feeling of recognition.

questions.q: After the scandal, the minister was left to face the music.
questions.tip: 'Face the music' means to accept unpleasant results.

questions.q: My mother turned a blind eye to the biscuit tin being emptied.
questions.tip: 'Turned a blind eye' means deliberately ignored.

questions.q: The two shops are cutting corners to keep prices low.
questions.tip: 'Cutting corners' means doing something poorly to save time or money.

questions.q: He has been burning the midnight oil before the examination.
questions.tip: 'Burning the midnight oil' means working late.

questions.q: That excuse does not hold water.
questions.tip: 'Does not hold water' means cannot be believed.

questions.q: She got cold feet just before the audition.
The two of them see eye to eye on almost nothing.
questions.tip: 'See eye to eye' means to agree.

questions.q: His remark about her cooking really put his foot in it.
questions.tip: 'Put his foot in it' means said something tactless.

questions.q: The team was over the moon after reaching the final.
I smell a rat in this arrangement.
questions.tip: 'Smell a rat' means to suspect trickery.

questions.q: Our plans went up in smoke when the venue was flooded.
questions.tip: 'Went up in smoke' means were ruined.

questions.q: The new rule has caused a storm in a teacup.
questions.tip: 'A storm in a teacup' means an overreaction to a trivial matter.

questions.q: He was caught red-handed taking the coins.
Winning that match was a feather in her cap.
options: an achievement to be proud of
questions.m: an achievement to be proud of
a: an achievement to be proud of
questions.tip: 'A feather in her cap' means an honour.

questions.q: The two sisters are as thick as thieves.
questions.tip: 'As thick as thieves' means extremely close friends.

questions.q: He bit off more than he could chew by joining four clubs.
questions.tip: 'Bit off more than he could chew' means undertook too much.

questions.q: Their argument was just a drop in the ocean compared with the real problem.
questions.tip: 'A drop in the ocean' means insignificant in comparison.

questions.q: The prefect turned the tables on his accusers.
questions.tip: 'Turned the tables' means reversed the advantage.

questions.q: She always keeps her cards close to her chest.
questions.tip: 'Keeps her cards close to her chest' means keeps plans secret.

questions.q: The new timetable has thrown a spanner in the works.
questions.tip: 'Thrown a spanner in the works' means disrupted a plan.

questions.q: He is a chip off the old block.
questions.tip: 'A chip off the old block' means closely resembling a parent.

questions.q: We will have to play it by ear on the day.
Whether pupils may use their phones during breaks is a grey area in the rules.
questions.tip: 'A grey area' means something not clearly defined.

questions.q: After the third delay, we were at the end of our tether.
questions.tip: 'At the end of our tether' means unable to endure more.

questions.q: He let sleeping dogs lie and said nothing about the old quarrel.
questions.tip: 'Let sleeping dogs lie' means avoid stirring up trouble.

questions.q: The captain was thrown in at the deep end on her first match.
options: given a hard task with no preparation
questions.m: given a hard task with no preparation
a: given a hard task with no preparation
questions.tip: 'Thrown in at the deep end' means made to start with the hardest part.

questions.q: The video was unknown on Monday; by Friday she had become famous overnight.
questions.tip: 'Overnight' means very suddenly, in a very short time.

sets.title: Precise words & abstract nouns · 40 items
sets.instruction: Choose the word that says exactly what is meant. These are the words that lift a Primary 6 composition.

questions.q: Her __________ in the face of the illness impressed the nurses.
questions.tip: 'Fortitude' means courage in bearing pain or trouble.

questions.q: He acted out of pure __________ and expected nothing in return.
questions.tip: 'Generosity' is the noun for giving freely.

questions.q: The __________ of the old library was its silence.
They were united by a shared __________ of purpose.
questions.tip: 'A sense of purpose' is the set phrase.

questions.q: His __________ to finish the race despite the injury astonished us.
The committee questioned the __________ of the decision.
She showed great __________ in admitting her error publicly.
The __________ between the two accounts troubled the teacher.
His __________ was clear from the way he kept checking the door.
questions.tip: 'Apprehension' means anxiety about what may happen.

questions.q: The boy's __________ won him few friends.
questions.tip: 'Arrogance' means an exaggerated sense of one's own importance.

questions.q: There was an air of __________ in the hall before the results.
questions.tip: 'Anticipation' means expectation of something about to happen.

questions.q: Her __________ made the newcomers feel welcome at once.
The __________ of the task did not discourage him.
His __________ to the team never wavered in ten years.
They acted with complete __________ for the safety rules.
questions.tip: 'Disregard' means paying no attention to something.

questions.q: The __________ of his apology was obvious to everyone.
A sudden __________ came over the crowd as the anthem began.
Her __________ of the situation was better than mine.
The __________ of the decision was felt for years afterwards.
He spoke with an __________ that silenced the room.
She met the criticism with quiet __________.
The __________ of losing was harder to bear than the loss itself.
The cleaner worked with a __________ that left not one corner dusty.
His __________ about the plan turned out to be justified.
questions.tip: 'Scepticism' means doubt about whether something is true.

questions.q: The essay lacked __________ and jumped between ideas.
She drew __________ from her grandmother's example.
questions.tip: 'Inspiration' means the encouragement to act or create.

questions.q: There was no __________ in his voice when he made the promise.
questions.tip: 'Hesitation' means a pause caused by uncertainty.

questions.q: The __________ of the two systems made comparison unfair.
He bore the disappointment with unusual __________ for a nine-year-old.
Her __________ for stray animals was known throughout the estate.
The __________ of the evidence convinced even the doubters.
questions.tip: 'The weight of the evidence' means its persuasive force.

questions.q: She questioned the __________ of blaming a single pupil.
The report exposed a serious __________ in the safety checks.
His __________ to change his mind cost the team the match.
There is a certain __________ in doing a task properly.
The __________ of his argument was that nobody had asked the pupils.
She acted on __________ rather than on any plan.
The __________ of the neighbourhood changed after the market closed.
questions.tip: 'Character' here means the distinctive quality of a place.

questions.q: His story was met with open __________.
questions.tip: 'Disbelief' means refusal to accept something as true.

questions.q: The volunteers worked with unfailing __________ for six hours.

sets.title: Vocabulary cloze · two passages
sets.instruction: One word only for each blank. The word must fit the meaning and the grammar. Read both passages right through before you begin.

passages.text:
Passage A — The Man Who Fixed Umbrellas

For thirty-one years, Mr Chua kept a (1)______ no wider than a doorway at the edge of the market.

He (2)______ umbrellas, and nothing else.

His (3)______ brought him bent ribs, torn canopies and handles that had snapped in the wind.

He worked slowly and (4)______, never once losing his temper with a tangled rib.

He (5)______ two dollars for a small repair and never more than five for a large one.

It was often (6)______ to buy a new umbrella than to have an old one mended.

When people said so, he (7)______ that a new umbrella would break in the same place.

He had a few dozen (8)______ customers who had been coming to him since the nineteen nineties.

Last March, at the age of seventy-eight, he finally (9)______.

On his last afternoon there was a (10)______ outside the stall for the first time in years.

People (11)______ him biscuits, coffee and umbrellas that did not need repairing.

Nobody in the market has taken up his (12)______.

The stall stands (13)______ now, with the shutters down.

The older stallholders still (14)______ the sound of his sewing machine at seven in the morning.

It was, they say, the quietest (15)______ in the noisiest place in Singapore.

Passage B — Why Nobody Wants the Window Seat

On a school bus, the best seat seems (16)______: the window seat, with a view and a wall to lean on.

Yet if you (17)______ a bus of primary school children for a week, you will notice something odd.

The older pupils (18)______ it, and the younger ones fight over it.

The (19)______ has nothing to do with the view.

A pupil in the window seat is (20)______ until whoever is beside them stands up.

The aisle seat, by contrast, gives you (21)______ over when you leave.

For a Primary 1 pupil that hardly (22)______, because the journey is an adventure.

For a Primary 6 pupil on a (23)______ bus that is about to reach the school gate, it matters a great deal.

The preference therefore reverses (24)______ over six years, without anybody discussing it.

The bus driver, Mr Selamat, has (25)______ this for twenty years.

He says the little ones (26)______ the window before they have even reached the step.

The (27)______ ones, he says, walk straight past it without looking.

answers.tip: The title and 'no wider than a doorway' point to a tiny market shop, which a 'stall' is.
The title tells us he mended umbrellas, so a past-tense verb is needed; 'mended' or 'fixed' fit too.
The people who 'brought him' broken umbrellas are his customers, and 'His' needs a plural noun.
The slot pairs with the adverb 'slowly' and is explained by never losing his temper.
Prices are named, so a past-tense verb about asking for money fits; 'paid' would reverse who pays.
'Than' shows a comparison, so a comparative adjective is needed, and buying new costs less than mending.
He gives a reason after 'that', so a past-tense speech verb is needed; 'replied' would also work.
Customers coming since the nineties come often, so an adjective meaning frequent fits; 'loyal' works too.
'Finally', his age of seventy-eight and the closed stall show he stopped working for good.
People lined up on his last afternoon, so a noun for a line of waiting people fits; 'crowd' works too.
They gave him gifts, so a past-tense verb of giving is needed, and 'brought' is the past of 'bring'.
'Taken up' needs a noun for his skilled line of work; 'business' would also fit here.
'Shutters down' shows the stall is now unused, so an adjective meaning unoccupied fits; 'closed' works too.
'Still' with a present-tense verb about the past means they recall the sound; 'recall' fits too.
A noun naming his line of work is needed again, contrasting his quiet mending with the noisy market.
'Seems' needs an adjective, and the colon explains a choice that is plain to see.
'If you' needs a present-tense verb about watching carefully for a week; 'watch' would also fit.
The older pupils act oppositely to the younger ones who fight over it, so a verb meaning shun fits.
The slot before 'has nothing to do with the view' needs a noun meaning the explanation.
'Until whoever is beside them stands up' shows the pupil cannot get out, so an adjective meaning stuck fits.
'Gives you ______ over when you leave' needs a noun meaning the power to decide.
'Hardly' and the later 'it matters a great deal' show a present-tense verb meaning is important.
Getting out is hard when the bus is full, so an adjective like 'crowded' or 'packed' fits.
The change happens slowly across six years, so an adverb of manner is needed, not an adjective.
'Has ______ this for twenty years' needs a past participle about observing; 'seen' would also fit.
The little ones rush to take the window seat, so a present-tense verb meaning grab for themselves fits.
These pupils are contrasted with 'the little ones', so a comparative adjective about age is needed.
'Less a choice than a ______ they grow into' needs a noun for behaviour learnt over time.
'Refuses a window ______' needs the noun the whole passage is about, matching 'window seat' earlier.
After 'are simply' an '-ing' verb is needed, and thinking ahead about leaving is what they do.
